questions.question: Outline how the Term 1 project followed the design process, naming what was produced at each of the five steps.
questions.expected_answer: Investigate: the scenario was turned into a problem statement, levers and mechanical advantage were studied and the syringe investigations produced a results table, ending in a design brief. Design: a brief with specifications and constraints, fitness-for-purpose considerations, several labelled sketches, a chosen design with reasons, an oblique drawing and a dimensioned working drawing with a parts list. Make: a sequence of manufacture and the cardboard and syringe model built safely to the drawing. Evaluate: tests against each specification with measurements and proposed improvements. Communicate: the design record throughout and a presentation of the model and the principle it shows.

questions.question: Compare the three classes of lever and explain, using the rescue device, how both levers and hydraulics multiplied the force.
questions.expected_answer: First class has the pivot in the middle, reverses direction and can have any mechanical advantage; second class has the load in the middle and always has MA greater than 1; third class has the effort in the middle and always has MA less than 1 but gives speed and reach. In the rescue device, water pushed from a small syringe into a larger one produced a greater force at the larger plunger in proportion to the piston areas, a hydraulic advantage, and that push on the back ends of two first-class arms, with the pivot nearer the jaw tips than the back ends, was multiplied again by the ratio of the arms, at the cost of a smaller movement at the tips.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a working drawing and an oblique drawing, and list three pairs of ideas from the term that learners often confuse, with the distinction for each.
questions.expected_answer: A working drawing shows one face flat and to scale, carries every real dimension in millimetres and is used for making; an oblique drawing shows the true front face with depth receding at 45 degrees on squared paper, is used for showing the whole object and is not dimensioned along its receding lines. Confused pairs: load, the force moved, versus effort, the force applied; specification, a testable feature of the product, versus constraint, a limit on the project; cost-effectiveness, value for money, versus cheapness; hydraulics, an incompressible liquid giving firm immediate response, versus pneumatics, a compressible gas giving springy delayed response; evaluation, measured results against the brief, versus praise.
